notes: עַל־מָה fuses as 'Why' under rule 30, leaving the fronted 'do' to the participle under rule 17's limit for an interrogative with an English word of its own.
עָרֵי הַמִּבְצָר is rule 29's fronting case joined to rule 28: the rectum is rendered attributively and anarthrously as 'fortified', so its present article takes the single written 'the'.

Both light-verb renderings head on their complements under rule 44 — 'hath put … to silence' on 'silence' and 'given … to drink' on 'drink' — each discontinuous around the object suffix's own pronoun.
The Niphal imperative keeps 'yourselves' as its own voice under rule 44, and the two cohortatives keep their supplied 'let us'.
